title_original: Skydance merging WB, Paramount TV studios

blocks.text: Skydance is merging Warner Bros Television Group (WBTV) and Paramount Television Studios (PTVS) under the single banner Warner Bros Television Studios that launches in early 2027.

Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell, who ran WBTV and PTVS, respectively, will serve as presidents of the new business, reporting to Skydance TV co-chair and chief content officer George Cheeks. The two presidents will oversee BET Studios and Warner Bros International Television Production.

Both TV studios will operate separately until launch. Cheeks did not mention redundancies in an internal memo to staff announcing the news on Wednesday. Skydance carries a debt load of $80bn and top brass are looking to make $6bn in cuts in the next three years.
Dungey remains chair of Skydance Global Cable Media encompassing Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery’s cable network stable of more than 50 brands.
CBS Studios led by David Stapf will remain a standalone and comprises CBS Studios International, Skydance Sports Entertainment and See It Now Studios.
“Bringing these teams together gives us an even stronger foundation to support storytellers, champion great ideas and bring exceptional television to audiences around the world,” Cheeks said.
Earlier this week Skydance announced its film leadership structure.
